points.description: States that the child's kernel context/kernel stack is set up by the kernel (during fork) so that when the child is first scheduled it begins executing in kernel mode at the start of a specific function (e.g., forkret), via its saved context.
States that the child's kernel stack is prepared so that the return address of that starting function is the trap handler's return code (e.g., trapret).
States that when the child is scheduled it runs that function and returns from it to the trap-return address, i.e. it returns into the trap return path without any real trap having occurred.
States that this emulates a call to and return from the trap handler, after which the rest of the kernel stack is unwound (trap frame restored) to return to user space.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four elements stated precisely: the context starts at a function like forkret, the kernel stack return address is trapret, the child returns from the function to that address, and this emulates a trap return that unwinds the stack to user mode. Vague statements such as 'the child just returns to user mode' or 'it copies the parent's trap frame' earn nothing alone. A wrong claim in a point (e.g., saying the child actually takes a trap) earns nothing for that point.
